blocks.text: PRIEST AND JUDGE OF ISRAEL · THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL
Eli. The priest at Shiloh who judged Israel forty years.
LED ISRAELi
40 years No years BC in Scripture
TRIBE
Levi (a priest)
IN THE LINE
14th of 15
SCRIPTURE SAYS
“Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD.”
PROPHETS
A man of God (not named) · Samuel
THE TRIBES OF ISRAEL: 15 RULERS MOSES → SAMUEL
SUCCESSION
Before and after
WHAT SCRIPTURE SAYS
What Scripture says of him
"Eli the priest sat upon a seat by a post of the temple of the LORD." 1 Samuel 1:9
He blessed Hannah: "the God of Israel grant thee thy petition". 1 Samuel 1:17
He heard what his sons did and asked, "Why do ye such things?", but "they hearkened not unto the voice of their father". 1 Samuel 2:22–25
God's charge against him: "his sons made themselves vile, and he restrained them not". 1 Samuel 3:13
His answer to the judgment: "It is the LORD: let him do what seemeth him good." 1 Samuel 3:18
"His heart trembled for the ark of God." 1 Samuel 4:13
The man of God said Eli honoured his sons above the LORD, and that his house would lose its old men and its place. 1 Samuel 2:29–33
The word was fulfilled when Solomon removed Abiathar from the priesthood. 1 Kings 2:27

Shiloh and the places of the story

THE NATION
What the nation did
Israel went up yearly to sacrifice at Shiloh, where Eli's sons were priests. 1 Samuel 1:3
"The word of the LORD was precious in those days; there was no open vision." 1 Samuel 3:1
The elders fetched the ark into battle, hoping "it may save us". 1 Samuel 4:3–5

ON THE WORLD STAGE
The powers of the day
THE PHILISTINES
DATES DIFFER
When was it?
SCRIPTURE'S OWN NUMBERS
No years given
Forty years in the Hebrew and the KJV (1 Samuel 4:18); the Greek (LXX) reads twenty. No year BC is given.
Forty, as in the Hebrew
Keil (1866)
Keil holds that the Greek reading twenty "does not deserve the slightest notice", since Eli would then have become judge at seventy-eight.[11]
Twenty, as in the Greek (LXX)
Moore (1895)
Moore adopts the Greek twenty, so that Samson's twenty and Eli's twenty fill the Philistines' forty years.[19]

WHAT SCRIPTURE DOES NOT SAY
Scripture does not say how Eli became priest or judge, or that he ever led an army.
1 Samuel does not name Eli's father; his descent from Ithamar is an inference (see identifications).
Scripture records no burial for Eli.
IDENTIFICATIONS THIS PAGE RELIES ON

Scholars' viewEli's descent from Aaron's son Ithamar is inferred: his great-grandson Ahimelech (1 Samuel 14:3; 22:20) is "of the sons of Ithamar" in 1 Chronicles 24:3. Keil draws this inference. 1 Samuel 14:3 1 Samuel 22:20 1 Chronicles 24:3 [10]
